case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth SIG qualification planning for a new automotive Bluetooth design that intends to reuse existing Qualcomm-qualified Bluetooth components. The main focus is determining whether a Controller Subsystem qualification can be created by adding RF and RF PHY evidence to an existing controller design and then combining it with an existing host design. During planning, a qualification blocker related to LE Class 1 consistency requirements and the new Bluetooth SIG qualification system is identified. The discussion also covers qualification strategy, test scope, registration constraints, and the practical impact of the post-July-2024 qualification workflow.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A key issue is that the selected controller design was qualified with LE Class 1 support enabled, creating a dependency that RF PHY qualification evidence must also indicate Class 1 support. If the new module operates below the required LE Class 1 transmit power range, combining it with the referenced controller design creates an inter-layer consistency problem. The team explored whether a Subset ID could be used to remove the Class 1 capability from the referenced component, but testing showed that the new qualification system would not allow the Subset ID to be included in the intended registration flow. The resulting conclusion was that a new component qualification reflecting the desired capability state would be required rather than relying on a subset workaround.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is driven by Bluetooth SIG consistency requirements between declared layer capabilities and the designs being combined. When a referenced controller design declares LE Class 1 support, dependent RF PHY qualification evidence and layer relationships must remain consistent. If the module's actual RF characteristics do not satisfy the referenced design's Class 1 declaration, the qualification combination becomes invalid. Because the qualification system would not permit the intended Subset ID reuse path, the inconsistency cannot be resolved through a subset-based workaround and must instead be corrected at the source design level.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Selecting a controller design whose LE Class 1 declarations do not match the module's actual RF capabilities can prevent successful completion of the Bluetooth qualification process due to inter-layer consistency failures. Relying on an unusable Subset ID strategy could result in qualification planning rework, additional coordination with the component supplier, redesign of the qualification approach, and project schedule delays. Delayed validation of host-controller-design combinations could also result in discovering qualification incompatibilities late in the project.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Before building a Bluetooth qualification strategy around reused QDIDs, DNs, component designs, or subsets, verify that all critical ICS and capability declarations remain consistent across every referenced layer. For post-2024 Bluetooth qualification workflows, confirm that proposed subset-based mitigation strategies are actually supported by the qualification tools before committing to a qualification plan.
